standard.title: Specification for Plain Hard-Drawn Steel Wire for Prestressed Concrete — Part 1: Cold Drawn Stress-Relieved Wire (Second Revision) [1]
standard.description: This standard specifies requirements for manufacture, chemical composition, physical properties, and testing of plain hard-drawn steel wires of nominal diameters from 2.50 mm up to 8.00 mm intended for use in pre-tensioned and post-tensioned prestressed concrete components [1].
standard.scope: This standard specifies requirements for manufacture, chemical composition, physical properties, and testing of plain hard-drawn steel wires of nominal diameters from 2.50 mm up to 8.00 mm intended for use in pre-tensioned and post-tensioned prestressed concrete components [1].

amendments.summary: Incorporates minor editorial and dimensional adjustments.
Updates formatting, testing protocols, and reference indexes.
Reduces maximum allowed Sulphur and Phosphorus content in the ladle analysis from 0.050 percent to 0.040 percent to ensure superior mechanical steel quality.

Inserts nominal wire diameters of 3.00 mm (tolerance ±0.04 mm, nominal mass 55.5 ± 1.5 g/m, minimum tensile strength 1865 N/mm²) and 2.50 mm (tolerance ±0.025 mm, nominal mass 38.5 ± 1.25 g/m, minimum tensile strength 2010 N/mm²) into Clauses 5.1, 5.1.2, 6.1, and 6.4 [1, 2].

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all plain hard-drawn steel wires for prestressed concrete must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial wire products as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Prestressing steel wires conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) stamped permanently on a metal tag attached to each wire coil.

Cold-drawn stress-relieved wires must satisfy high-tensile thresholds: nominal diameter of 3.00 mm must meet a minimum tensile strength of 1865 N/mm² [2], while nominal diameter of 2.50 mm must meet a minimum tensile strength of 2010 N/mm² [2].

Manufactured wires must satisfy precise dimensional limits: nominal diameter 3.00 mm has a tolerance of ±0.04 mm and corresponding nominal mass of 55.5 ± 1.5 g/m [1, 2]; nominal diameter 2.50 mm has a tolerance of ±0.025 mm and corresponding nominal mass of 38.5 ± 1.25 g/m [1, 2].

The wire must exhibit high cold ductility, passing the wrapping test (no fractures when wrapped 8 turns around its own diameter) and satisfying minimum total elongation-at-fracture values under Clause 6.4 [2].

To guarantee structural stability, the wire must undergo a mandatory long-term isothermal stress-relaxation test at 20 °C, verifying that relaxation losses under an initial tension equal to 70% of minimum tensile strength do not exceed specified limits.

High-carbon steel chemical constituents must be verified via ladle analysis: Carbon limits, Manganese, and restricted maximum Sulphur and Phosphorus content (restricted to <= 0.040 percent each) to prevent brittleness.
